item.title: Paramount Settles Lawsuits With States Clearing the Way to Buy WBD
item.description: Paramount Skydance settles lawsuits with 12 states clearing the way for it to buy Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. The deal limits Paramount's market power and it promises to release 30 movies a year at the combined studios. Charlie Pellett has the breaking news. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed's Musalem says more rate hikes likely needed to quell inflation
item.description: The Federal Reserve will likely need to hike interest rates further to lower inflation resulting from strong demand as well as a commodity price shock that has moved beyond oil, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Monday, adding that it would be better for the US central bank to act sooner than wait.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve will likely need to hike interest rates further to lower inflation resulting from strong demand as well as a commodity price shock that has moved beyond oil, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Monday, adding that it would be better for the US central bank to act sooner than wait. "Both persistent demand and recurring supply forces are continuing to contribute to keeping inflation risks elevated, and I judge that without further policy restraint on inflation it is more likely to be substantially above our 2% target in 18 months than at target," Musalem said in an interview with Reuters. "I think it's crucial that policy puts a meaningful restraint on inflation" so the Fed reaches its inflation target in about a year and a half, allowing time for tighter policy to impact the economy, he said. Musalem, who is not currently a voting member of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, would not comment on the Fed's possible next steps or the estimated level the policy rate may need to reach to lower inflation. But "earlier and incremental policy firming is better and less disruptive than later and larger and potentially more abrupt policy action" further in the future, he said. Inflation "is not a risk. It's there," Musalem said, noting that even after stripping out the impact of oil and other supply-related factors, underlying inflation is running perhaps a percentage point above the Fed's target and is "moving in the wrong direction." Little progress has been made recently in the battle to bring inflation back down to the 2% target. The [USN:L1N44N0KC TEXT:"Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index"], the Fed's main inflation gauge, was at 3.7% on a year-over-year basis in July, compared to a recent low of 2.3% in April of 2025, as the Trump administration rolled out its plan for global import tariffs. The shock to import prices was followed this year by the start of the US-Israeli [USN:L1N45D0B1 TEXT:"war with Iran"], which pushed up fuel costs globally, with the price of diesel hitting a record high recently. Prices for commodities like copper have also been rising, Musalem said, as an offshoot of the artificial intelligence investment boom. Through it all, US domestic spending and growth have remained resilient — good news from one perspective, but an additional inflation challenge for the Fed. "We have both strong demand forces and supply forces working themselves through the economy," Musalem said. 'LABOR MARKET IS NOT A SOURCE OF INFLATION' The Fed last [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised interest rates"] by a quarter of a percentage point last week and dropped a reference in its policy statement that attributed recent inflation "in part" to supply shocks, saying only that "inflation remains elevated." The change reflects growing skepticism at the central bank that current price pressures are likely to fade over time without Fed action. Though things like tariffs and [USN:L1N45C06F TEXT:"oil price increases"] were seen as potentially fleeting, one-off changes in the price level, their influence has proved more persistent than expected, with inflation now being driven by demand aspects as well. "I think there's a recognition that consumption and investment are growing at a very healthy, very strong clip, and at the same time the risks on the inflation side seem to have increased for a variety of reasons, including geopolitical forces," Musalem said. The St. Louis Fed chief said he views the current 3.75%-4.00% policy rate as "on the accommodative side," meaning it is not yet high enough to restrict economic activity. Investors currently expect the Fed to approve three more quarter-percentage-point rate hikes over the five policy meetings between now and April, with roughly even odds the central bank will hike again in October, on the eve of the US midterm elections. The [USN:L6N45816B TEXT:"median projection"] of Fed officials issued after last week's meeting showed policymakers anticipate one more hike this year, with a near-even split over the need for another such move in 2027, a less aggressive outcome than investors currently anticipate. Though tighter policy may be needed, Musalem said he did not think it would need to come at the cost of higher unemployment, or that it would boost the likelihood of a recession. "The [USN:L1N44W0EC TEXT:"labor market"] is not a source of inflation. There's not necessarily a need to slow the labor market down or to cool it to attain our inflation target," Musalem said, with the job market "stable and balanced and around full employment." But he said he hoped businesses would scale back the pace of price increases that contacts in his Fed district say are on the horizon. Firms are "reporting sharply higher non-labor input costs, in fuel and other raw materials, transportation, insurance, and skilled labor," Musalem said. "They're planning to raise their selling prices. ... There is ample evidence that inflation is the principal problem we have right now."

item.title: Falcons staying mum on QB front with Thursday game looming
item.description: The Atlanta Falcons don't have much time to figure out their shaky quarterback situation with a Thursday game at the Green Bay Packers looming this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Falcons don't have much time to figure out their shaky quarterback situation with a Thursday game at the Green Bay Packers looming this week. Atlanta coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters he likely knows who will start but didn't share details on Monday. "I have a decent idea of where we're going, but I haven't spoken to players yet," Stefanski said. NFL Network and ESPN reported Sunday that Michael Penix Jr., the Falcons' first-round pick (eighth overall) in the 2024 NFL Draft, could make his season debut for Atlanta (0-2) against Green Bay (1-1). He has been sidelined since last November, when he suffered an ACL tear, but told reporters last week he was "really close" to returning. Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with Atlanta in the offseason, could also be available after he was inactive for the first two games of the season with an oblique injury suffered days before the team's season opener at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cooper Rush started the first two games with the top two options out, completing 56.4% of his passes for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions before he was benched during Sunday's 34-3 home loss to the Carolina Panthers. Undrafted rookie Jack Strand replaced Rush, completing 8 of 15 passes for 59 yards and an interception -- which was returned for a touchdown -- in his regular-season debut. He could be in line for his first career start if Penix and Tagovailoa are still unavailable against the Packers. --Field Level Media

MUMBAI: The National Stock Exchange of India's IPO drew more than US$10 billion by the final day of bidding on Monday (Sep 21), as investors look to tap into a boom in public listing s in Asia's third-largest economy. The US$2.3 billion IPO , the country's biggest after Hyundai Motor India's HYUN.NS $3.3 billion offering, received bids for 505.81 million shares, 5.71 times the 88.64 million shares on offer after three days of bidding, exchange data showed. NSE shares will likely begin trading on Thursday, marking the culmination of a decade-long effort by India’s biggest stock exchange operator to enter public markets. The IPO comes at a time when India's primary market is picking up, with billion aire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms likely to list later this year in what could be the country's biggest-ever stock offering.

Qualified institutional buyers led demand at the NSE IPO , bidding for 12.68 times the number of shares set aside for them. Non-institutional and retail investor portions were subscribed 6.55 times and 1.39 times, respectively. The strong institutional demand signals investors' willingness to look past a recent slowdown in the derivatives segment and bet on long-term growth prospects for the Indian capital market, analysts said. India's largest bourse has a 93 per cent share in the cash market and nearly 75 per cent in options. Investors on the exchange jumped 40 per cent over two years to 129.09 million as of March end. However, regulatory tightening, taxation and a new closing auction have hit derivatives trading. "The decline in derivatives volume is a phenomenon that has been playing out since 2024.... From a long-term perspective, the volumes should still trend higher and NSE 's smaller businesses outside the derivatives segment should also be able to contribute materially to earnings," said Vipul Bhowar, executive director and head of equities at Waterfield Advisors in Mumbai.

GREY MARKET HINTS AT LISTING GAINS The premium for NSE shares in the grey market indicate gains of 2 per cent to 5 per cent on trading debut. The grey market is an unregulated market that allows investors to trade IPO shares before the official listing . NSE has set a price band of 1,700 rupees to 1,785 rupees apiece for its shares and is seeking a valuation of up to US$46 billion , which is 15 per cent to 20 per cent lower than the valuation sought in pre-deal roadshows. "The lower-than-anticipated valuation limits the downside risk for NSE and if the stock falls below IPO price after listing , it should be seen as a buying opportunity," Bhowar said.

item.title: AI could boost LatAm, Caribbean economy 5.1% but wages may fall, IDB says
item.description: Broad adoption of artificial intelligence could leave the economy of Latin America and the Caribbean 5.1% larger after a decade, but wages could fall by as much as 20.9% if workers cannot move into jobs expanding with AI, according to forthcoming research from the Inter-American Development Bank.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: Broad adoption of artificial intelligence could leave the economy of Latin America and the Caribbean 5.1% larger after a decade, but wages could fall by as much as 20.9% if workers cannot move into jobs expanding with AI, according to forthcoming research from the Inter-American Development Bank. The IDB’s 2026 flagship report, due in November, estimates that regional GDP could be only 0.3% higher under limited adoption and small productivity gains. Wages could increase by 2.3% to 5.3% if workers move into jobs in expanding sectors, but fall by 13.5% to 20.9% if they cannot. The IDB is the largest development lender in Latin America and the Caribbean and has 48 member countries, including 26 borrowing members in the region. IDB President Ilan Goldfajn also called for more financing, long-term purchase contracts and minimum-price protection for critical-minerals supply chains. He said minerals produced in ways that respect labor conditions and the environment should be differentiated from supply produced without those safeguards and referred to a minimum price for buyers as a “buyers’ club.” Goldfajn, who was due to discuss AI and critical minerals with regional leaders and technology executives on Monday, gave no details on how the club or price mechanism would work, who might participate or whether the IDB would provide financial backing.

item.title: Kaitlin Quevedo wins at Sao Paulo for first WTA title
item.description: Kaitlin Quevedo of Spain turned a dominating burst to open the third set into a 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 victory over Nadia Podoroska of Argentina in the final of the SP Open at Sao Paulo, Brazil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kaitlin Quevedo of Spain turned a dominating burst to open the third set into a 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 victory over Nadia Podoroska of Argentina in the final of the SP Open at Sao Paulo, Brazil. It was the first career WTA tournament victory for Quevedo, who made her tour-level debut in January. Podoroska took the opening set by breaking Quevedo's serve twice in the opening three games. More trouble emerged when Quevedo again was broken to open the second set but she dominated from there while winning 62% of her second-serve returns and saving five of nine break points. Singapore Open No. 5 seed Maja Chwalinska of Poland earned an easy 6-4, 6-2 victory over wild-card Rebecca Sramkova of Slovakia in the first round as the French Open finalist looks to reignite the back half of her season. Chwalinska, who moved on from France to lose in the first round at Wimbledon and the U.S. Open, won the last four games of the second set to advance. No. 6 seed Leylah Fernandez of Canada earned a 6-2, 6-3 victory in the opening round over Kyoka Okamura of Japan. Joanna Garland of Taiwan and Talia Gibson of Australia also won first-round matches. Korea Open No. 3 seed Lanlana Tararudee finished off a 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2 victory over Moyuka Uchijima of Japan in the first round at Seoul, South Korea. No. 5 seed Maya Joint of Australia also advanced out of the first round with a 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-3 victory over China's Xinxin Yao, as did No. 8 seed Kamilla Rakhimova of Uzbekistan, who was a 7-6 (4), 4-6, 7-5 winner over countrywoman Polina Kudermetova. Also earning first-round victories were Dayeon Back of South Korea, Russia's Alina Korneeva and American Katie Volynets, while No. 7 seed Magda Linette of Poland fell 3-6, 6-1, 7-6 (2) to Darya Astakhova of Russia. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lula se encontra com Mamdani em Nova York às vésperas de importantes eleições
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se reuniu com o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, nesta segunda-feira, para uma primeira conversa entre duas das figuras mais importantes da esquerda política nas Américas, às vésperas de decisivas eleições tanto no Brasil quanto nos Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Teixeira
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se reuniu com o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, nesta segunda-feira, para uma primeira conversa entre duas das figuras mais importantes da esquerda política nas Américas, às vésperas de decisivas eleições tanto no Brasil quanto nos Estados Unidos. Lula viajou para os Estados Unidos para a Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas e recebeu Mamdani em uma casa no Upper East Side que serve como residência e escritório da representação brasileira na ONU. Lula disse, em uma breve declaração a jornalistas após o encontro, que os dois conversaram sobre problemas comuns aos dois países, especialmente o aumento do custo de vida. Mamdani disse que vai se inspirar nos programas sociais implementados por Lula no Brasil em sua busca por melhoras nas condições dos nova-iorquinos que enfrentam dificuldades financeiras com despesas principalmente de supermercado e aluguel. Lula concorre a um quarto mandato como presidente do Brasil, com o primeiro turno das eleições marcado para 4 de outubro. A maioria das pesquisas o mostra tecnicamente empatado com o senador de direita Flávio Bolsonaro, filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro e aliado do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. Mamdani tem sido uma figura central no Partido Democrata dos EUA, à medida que o país se aproxima de uma importante eleição de meio de mandato, em novembro, que pode alterar a composição do Congresso, levando a uma maior representação dos democratas. Lula e Mamdani trocaram camisetas de futebol após o encontro.

item.title: Stars sign F Sam Steel to 4-year, $14.8M extension
item.description: The Dallas Stars signed forward Sam Steel to a four-year, $14.8 million contract extension on Monday in a deal that starts with the 2027-28 season and carries an average annual value of $3.7 million.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Stars signed forward Sam Steel to a four-year, $14.8 million contract extension on Monday in a deal that starts with the 2027-28 season and carries an average annual value of $3.7 million. Steel, 28, set career highs in goals (12), assists (21) and points (33) in 73 games with the Stars in 2025-26. "We couldn't be happier to extend Sam," Dallas general manager Jim Nill said. "His consistency during his time with our team, especially on the penalty kill, plus his versatility has made him a valuable asset to our organization, and we're happy to be locking him up for the next four seasons." Steel has 175 points (61 goals, 114 assists) in 491 career games with the Anaheim Ducks (2018-22), Minnesota Wild (2022-23) and Stars. The Ducks drafted the Alberta native in the first round (30th overall) in 2016. Steel has 14 points (three goals, 11 assists) in 48 career playoff games and helped the Stars reach the Western Conference final in both 2023-24 and 2024-25. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nestle Russia pledges to continue operations despite Kremlin transfer of assets
item.description: Nestle's Russian subsidiary pledged to continue its operations in Russia without regard to a decision by the Kremlin to transfer control of the company's assets, the Swiss food giant was quoted as saying on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nestle's (NESN.S) Russian subsidiary pledged to continue its operations in Russia without regard to a decision by the Kremlin to transfer control of the company's assets, the Swiss food giant was quoted as saying on Monday. "The Nestle Group in Russia is continuing its commercial activities in Russia in full and wishes to state its intention to unconditionally fulfil all obligations to clients, partners, and employees," state news agency TASS quoted the company's Russian press service as saying in a statement in Russian. The Russian assets of Nestle and French retailer Auchan were, by virtue of a presidential decree on Friday, [USN:L8N45A06P TEXT:"transferred"] to temporary control by L.E.V. Management, a little-known company with no public profile. The Nestle statement quoted by TASS said the transfer did not amount to nationalisation or a change of ownership. It said Nestle expressed confidence that working with the team at L.E.V. Management would help the company continue to grow and improve its efficiency. After the presidential decree was announced last week, Nestle, maker of Nescafe coffee and KitKat chocolate bars, said it was "committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights and ensure continuity of business operations in the interests of all stakeholders, particularly its employees". The Kremlin said hostile actions by "unfriendly" countries played a role in its decision to take control of the Russian assets of Nestle and Auchan. In previous cases, temporary administration has often been followed by state expropriation, with assets later transferred to Kremlin-linked individuals or companies. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only temporary administration was under consideration for now.

item.title: Delegação liderada por presidente da Venezuela discutirá dívida e energia nos EUA, dizem fontes
item.description: Uma delegação venezuelana liderada pela presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez, que participa da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas nesta semana, planeja discutir questões relacionadas à energia, à dívida e à mineração com representantes dos Estados Unidos, informaram duas fontes que acompanham os preparativos.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga, Vivian Sequera
item.content:encoded: Uma delegação venezuelana liderada pela presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez, que participa da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas nesta semana, planeja discutir questões relacionadas à energia, à dívida e à mineração com representantes dos Estados Unidos, informaram duas fontes que acompanham os preparativos. A expectativa é que as negociações resultem na assinatura de acordos que integram os planos do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de reconstrução dos principais setores da economia do país sul-americano, segundo as fontes. Rodríguez chegou a Nova York na madrugada desta segunda-feira com sua equipe. Esta foi sua primeira viagem aos EUA após assumir o cargo de presidente interina da Venezuela em janeiro, sob supervisão de Washington, depois da captura do então presidente Nicolás Maduro pelas forças norte-americanas. O principal diplomata dos EUA na Venezuela, John Barrett, a recebeu no aeroporto, informou a TV estatal venezuelana. Ministros e autoridades venezuelanas de alto escalão vêm avançando nas negociações há meses que antecederam a viagem de Rodríguez a Nova York, onde ela deve se encontrar com Trump, na terça-feira. Nesta segunda-feira, Rodríguez tinha agendado um encontro com o secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, de acordo com a agenda dele. O encontro planejado entre Trump e Rodríguez -- que foi vice-presidente da Venezuela no governo de Maduro -- ocorrerá à margem de uma recepção oferecida pelo presidente dos EUA, informou o embaixador dos EUA na ONU, Mike Waltz, durante recente coletiva de imprensa por teleconferência. Os ministérios das Relações Exteriores e da Informação da Venezuela não responderam imediatamente a pedidos de comentários. Alguns prédios de propriedade da Venezuela em Nova York, incluindo um consulado e o escritório da missão do país na ONU, foram recentemente reformados, segundo reportagens. A ministra do Petróleo, Paula Henao, o ministro de Mineração, Héctor Silva, e altos funcionários da petrolífera estatal PDVSA participaram neste mês de uma conferência de energia do G20 em Houston, onde foi assinado um memorando de entendimento com a produtora de petróleo norte-americana Continental Resources para uma área na principal região produtora da Venezuela, o Cinturão do Orinoco. Também foi assinado um contrato separado concedendo à empresa de investimentos norte-americana Heeney Capital direitos operacionais e de exportação para uma mina de ouro. Outro acordo preliminar vem sendo negociado há meses com a gigante energética norte-americana ExxonMobil , o que poderia, em última instância, levar ao seu retorno aos campos petrolíferos da Venezuela, disseram fontes neste mês. Por sua vez, o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento está elaborando um plano de atuação de dois anos para a Venezuela, focado em parte em eletricidade e proteção social, disse à Reuters nesta segunda-feira seu presidente, Ilan Goldfajn. A iniciativa inclui missões para examinar a estrutura macroeconômica e os dados do país, assim como para estimar as necessidades de investimento em diferentes setores.

item.title: Trump administration sued over withheld federal grants for US community lenders
item.description: A business advocacy group representing government-backed community lenders sued the U.S. Treasury Department on Monday, seeking to prevent nearly $300 million in federal grants from expiring at the end of the month.
item.dc:creator: David Hood-Nuño
item.content:encoded: A business advocacy group representing government-backed community lenders sued the U.S. Treasury Department on Monday, seeking to prevent nearly $300 million in federal grants from expiring at the end of the month. The Washington-based Freedom Economy Business Association filed the suit in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, arguing the Treasury unlawfully failed to distribute fiscal year 2025 funding approved by Congress for Community Development Financial Institutions, or CDFIs. Because Congress appropriated the funds and CDFIs lawfully applied for them, they should be distributed, it said. The Treasury Department did not respond to a request for comment. CDFIs are specialized lenders that provide financing to small businesses, affordable housing projects, health clinics and other community initiatives that often lack access to traditional sources of capital. The Treasury certifies CDFIs and distributes grants authorized annually by Congress. The vast majority of CDFIs do not take deposits, meaning gvernment funding is a critical lifeline. While Treasury announced awards on September 15, it has not identified recipients or obligated the funds, leaving the money at risk of expiring when the fiscal year ends on September 30, Freedom Economy said. The group has asked the court to order Treasury and the Office of Manaagement and Budget to distribute funds before the deadline and to move forward with an additional $289 million appropriated by Congress for fiscal year 2026. It also asked the court for a temporary restraining order to immediately prevent Treasury from "running out the clock," according to Alphonso David, CEO of the Global Black Economic Forum and lead counsel in the case. The Trump administration last year said the organizations promoted a "partisan agenda," "gender extremism" and "climate radicalism," claims they deny. The funding delay led one CDFI to shutter and further delays could cause more to close, community lenders have warned. CDFIs have laid off staff, downsized operations and accrued debt, Tynesia Boyea-Robinson, chair of Freedom Economy, told reporters at a press conference. "Many of our members are unable to serve the millions of people relying on them," she said. "This is all because the federal government has refused to follow the law and meet their obligations under the law." The group expects a response from the courts within 48 hours, David said.

item.title: Oura, fabricante de anéis inteligentes, mira avaliação de US$15,6 bi em IPO
item.description: A Oura iniciou sua série de roadshows nesta segunda-feira para sua oferta pública inicial (IPO) nos Estados Unidos, com o objetivo de atingir uma avaliação totalmente diluída de US$15,62 bilhões. A fabricante de anéis inteligentes testa o apetite dos investidores por empresas de tecnologia de consumo após um início morno na temporada de IPOs do outono do hemisfério norte.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini
item.content:encoded: A Oura iniciou sua série de roadshows nesta segunda-feira para sua oferta pública inicial (IPO) nos Estados Unidos, com o objetivo de atingir uma avaliação totalmente diluída de US$15,62 bilhões. A fabricante de anéis inteligentes testa o apetite dos investidores por empresas de tecnologia de consumo após um início morno na temporada de IPOs do outono do hemisfério norte. A oferta pública inicial (IPO), prevista para a próxima semana, ocorre em um momento em que os mercados estão tensos nas últimas semanas devido à incerteza em torno do setor de inteligência artificial, ao aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos e à mudança nas perspectivas de taxas de juros do Federal Reserve. A Oura e alguns de seus investidores atuais planejam arrecadar até US$2,2 bilhões com a venda de 50 milhões de ações ao preço máximo da faixa indicada, de US$40 a US$44. "Oura é o primeiro teste real do apetite dos EUA após um setembro fraco até agora e um período de mercados mais voláteis. Se tiver um bom desempenho inicial, incentivará outros emissores", disse Samuel Kerr, chefe global de mercados de capitais de ações da Mergermarket. "No entanto, um IPO mais fraco pode soar o alarme, indicando que o sentimento do mercado pode estar mudando." A fabricante de medicamentos para perda de peso Eli Lilly (LLY.N) demonstrou interesse em adquirir até US$100 milhões em ações, enquanto a empresa de investimentos Dragoneer manifestou interesse em adquirir até US$300 milhões em ações. ALTA PROCURA POR MONITORES DE SAÚDE Os anéis inteligentes estão criando um nicho entre os rastreadores de fitness tradicionais e os relógios inteligentes, capitalizando a procura por informações de bem-estar personalizadas, ao mesmo tempo que oferecem uma forma mais compacta e sem tela de monitorar a saúde 24 horas por dia, com uma maior duração da bateria. A Oura ajudou a popularizar o dispositivo, que monitora métricas como saúde cardíaca, atividade física e sono. De acordo com o prospecto do IPO, a empresa de tecnologia da saúde vendeu 3,6 milhões de anéis Oura nos 12 meses encerrados em 30 de junho. Sua receita nos nove meses encerrados em 30 de junho aumentou aproximadamente 74% em relação ao ano anterior, atingindo US$1,21 bilhão. A empresa espera encerrar o ano fiscal de 2026 com aproximadamente 5,7 milhões de membros pagantes, o que representa um crescimento de 96% em relação ao ano anterior. "Um dos pontos fortes da Oura é que ele é fácil de usar para iniciantes, tem um design moderno e parece mais um acessório fácil de integrar ao dia a dia, em comparação com alguns dispositivos vestíveis voltados para atletas profissionais e monitoramento de desempenho", disse Kat Liu, vice-presidente da IPOX. "A avaliação claramente reflete um forte crescimento contínuo e uma maior transição para receitas recorrentes com margens mais elevadas." A empresa, fundada há mais de uma década na Finlândia, atingiu uma avaliação de cerca de 11 bilhões de dólares em uma rodada de financiamento em estágio avançado no ano passado. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley e JP Morgan são os principais bancos coordenadores do IPO. A empresa deverá definir o preço de seu IPO e começar a negociar na Nasdaq sob o código "OURA" na próxima semana.

item.title: Trump approval falls to career low of 32% as high costs bite, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to 32% - the lowest of his political career - as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living amid the unpopular Iran war, a new Reuters/Ipsos poll found.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to 32% - the lowest of his political career - as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living amid the unpopular Iran war, a new Reuters/Ipsos poll found. The four-day poll, which closed on Sunday, showed 73% of Republicans approved of Trump's job performance, down from 82% in a Reuters/Ipsos poll a week earlier. His overall approval stood at 35% that week. Trump returned to the White House in January 2025 on promises to tame inflation and end foreign wars. In a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in the hours after he was first sworn in, he enjoyed a 47% approval rate. Just 17% of respondents in the new poll approved of his handling of the cost of living - the top issue Americans say will determine how they vote in the November 3 midterm elections , when Trump's Republicans are defending narrow congressional majorities. Dissatisfaction among Republicans on the subject has been growing since Trump launched the war on Iran in February that has pushed gasoline and diesel prices sharply higher. Now for the first time, Republicans who disapprove of Trump's handling of the cost of living outnumber those who give him a thumbs up - 51% to 44%. The Reuters/Ipsos poll was conducted online and gathered 1,277 responses from US adults nationwide. It had a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Landmark NSE IPO threatens to hollow out Dalal Street’s shadow market
item.description: With the National Stock Exchange preparing for its listing, India's primary market is poised for significant enhancement. The landmark IPO is anticipated to trigger a marked decrease in the flourishing unlisted shares market, compelling platforms involved in these trades to identify alternative investment prospects.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: The landmark listing of National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. is set to deliver a major boost to the country’s primary market, but it will be a significant blow to the booming trade in unlisted shares.The operator of the world’s busiest derivatives market accounted for roughly half of the trading volume in the shadow market, according to an estimate by trading platform UnlistedZone. Its initial public offering threatens to trigger a sharp drop in activity, forcing platforms that facilitate such transactions to find the next big draw.As India set consecutive records in IPO proceeds the last two years, the unlisted market emerged as a venue for wealthy individuals and funds to make bet on companies in the listing pipeline. The booming interest fostered an ecosystem of online platforms and specialist brokers that specialize in connecting buyers and sellers.NSE had been a linchpin of the growing market because of its scale, profitability, dominant position and disclosures that mirrored listed companies. The presence of smaller listed rival BSE Ltd. gave investors a valuation benchmark, while years of delays in its listing meant an unusually long trading window.That helped turn a once-niche corner of India’s financial system into a mainstream investment avenue, giving rise to intermediaries that assisted investors with the regulatory approvals, documentation and transfers needed to buy shares.“NSE was quasi-listed,” said Sandipan Roy, chief investment officer at Motilal Oswal Private Wealth. “It spawned an entire industry.”The exchange had 231,378 shareholders ahead of its IPO, more than several listed companies. That compares with fewer than 80 shareholders it had in 2016, according to its December 2016 draft prospectus. Until last year, NSE made monthly disclosures on share transfers. Its last such release in March 2025 showed nearly 15 billion rupees ($170 million) of shares changing hands during the month.Staying relevant without NSE may prove more challenging for platforms that have mushroomed over the years. As no issuers currently offer the combination of size, familiarity and liquidity of NSE, they may have to persuade investors to trade smaller companies with typically less financial disclosure and thinner liquidity.“We expect interest in the unlisted market to remain selective as companies emerge across sectors such as space technology, aerospace, defense, data centers and other new-age industries,” said Rajan Shah, Founder, 3A Capital Services, which operates a platform for dealing in unlisted shares.Companies attracting market interest include Sterlite Electric Ltd, Indofil Industries Ltd, Krasny Defence Technologies Ltd, Berar Finance Ltd, Kineco Ltd, Indian Potash Ltd and Garuda Aerospace Ltd, he added.Investing in unlisted shares hasn’t always proved profitable. Investors in some high-profile names, including HDB Financial Services Ltd. and Tata Capital Ltd., suffered losses, while those who bought NSE shares over the past year may also enter the IPO sitting on losses.“There have also been instances of outsize returns in the unlisted market,” said Umesh Paliwal, co-founder, UnlistedZone. “Ultimately, entry timing and valuations are critical.”

item.title: Nicolas Batum announces basketball retirement at 37
item.description: Nicolas Batum announced his retirement on Monday following 1,205 games over 18 seasons with four NBA franchises.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nicolas Batum announced his retirement on Monday following 1,205 games over 18 seasons with four NBA franchises. The 37-year-old French forward averaged 9.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists with the Portland Trail Blazers (2008-15), Charlotte Hornets (2015-20), Los Angeles Clippers (2020-23, 2024-26) and Philadelphia 76ers (2023-24). Batum shared a video on social media to explain his decision. "After 21 years, it's time for me to go home," Batum said. "It's been 25 years since I left, 20 years as a pro. That's a lot. Eighteen years in the NBA, 15 with the French national team." Batum helped the French national team win Olympic silver medals in Tokyo (2020) and Paris (2024), and bronze medals at the FIBA World Cup in 2014 and 2019. The 6-foot-7 Batum was a first-round draft pick (25th overall) by the Houston Rockets in 2008 but was dealt to the Blazers in a draft night trade. He ranks tied for 29th in NBA history (with Donovan Mitchell) in 3-point field goals with 1,842. --Field Level Media

item.title: Saudi's Ceer unveils first EVs in bid to build regional auto powerhouse
item.description: Saudi startup Ceer made public its first two fully electric vehicle models on Monday and said it will launch five more models by 2030 as part of Saudi Arabia's goal to create a viable auto industry to curb the country's dependence on oil.
item.dc:creator: Ibraheemabu Mustafa, Nick Carey
item.content:encoded: Saudi startup Ceer made public its first two fully electric vehicle models on Monday and said it will launch five more models by 2030 as part of Saudi Arabia's goal to create a viable auto industry to curb the country's dependence on oil. Called Exobot, the futuristic premium electric sedan and SUV will start sales in Saudi Arabia in early 2027. With designs reminiscent of cars from sci-fi thriller "Tron", both vehicles have "gullwing" doors that open upward. Ceer has also removed the pillars normally found between a car's front and rear seats and relies instead on high-strength materials to provide structural support, Ceer CEO Jim DeLuca said. "We wanted to make sure the world could see what Saudi Arabia is capable of," he said. CHALLENGING TIMES TO LAUNCH NEW CARS Ceer's efforts to impress the market coincide with the greatest period of upheaval in the established car industry in the last century as [USN:L6N44S0I1 TEXT:"Chinese automakers"] take share from [USN:L8N45319B TEXT:"traditional rivals"] and lead the world in developing flashy new EVs. Ceer, a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund Public Investment Fund and Taiwanese contract electronics manufacturer Foxconn (2317.TW) , has the advantage of backing from the kingdom's oil wealth. But it still has to overcome the problems that have thwarted previous Saudi Arabian efforts to diversify into local car production and the logistics and inflationary problems linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran . Saudi Arabia's previous efforts include proposals for a Saudi-based Jaguar Land Rover factory that were abandoned over a decade ago. Toyota (7203.T) declined a deal in 2019, citing high labour costs and a lack of local suppliers. This time, Ceer has taken a broader approach, leaning on global partners and also a growing local network to provide parts. Foxconn has provided the electrical architecture for the Exobots, while German premium automaker BMW (BMWG.DE) provided engineering. Top-tier automotive suppliers, including U.S. firm Lear (LEA.N) , Korea's Shin Young, Germany's Benteler and China's Fangxin, have set up Saudi factories, encouraged by Saudi government incentives. Ceer is also taking a broad approach. Originally set up as a pure EV maker, its full lineup will include plug-in hybrids and combustion-engine models to react to shifting market demand, DeLuca said. Following the EV launch on Monday, Ceer will launch five mainstream models between 2028 and 2030. DeLuca said Ceer's upcoming mainstream models would be designed to meet all global regulatory requirements, so they could be ready for sale anywhere. The company aims to expand carefully through 2034, into surrounding markets in 2028 then across the Middle East and North Africa. "We want to make sure we move very methodically," DeLuca said. "It only takes one mistake and you can kill a startup." A number of EV startups including Fisker, Arrival and Lordstown have failed in the last few years. Vietnamese EV maker VinFast (VFS.O) , where DeLuca previously served as CEO, is restructuring after [USN:L6N41Y0HQ TEXT:"spending billions"] of dollars on expansion.

item.title: Arabia Saudita eleva exportación de petróleo por el golfo Pérsico tras ataque a oleoducto: datos
item.description: Saudi Aramco cargó el domingo unos 14 millones de barriles de crudo en siete superpetroleros en el Golfo Pérsico, según datos de TankerTrackers.com, en un contexto en que el reino está incrementando los despachos desde las terminales de exportación del golfo Pérsico tras un ataque que interrumpió los envíos a través de su oleoducto este-oeste hacia el mar Rojo.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Catherine Cartier, Enes Tunagur
item.content:encoded: Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) cargó el domingo unos 14 millones de barriles de crudo en siete superpetroleros en el Golfo Pérsico, según datos de TankerTrackers.com, en un contexto en que el reino está incrementando los despachos desde las terminales de exportación del golfo Pérsico tras un ataque que interrumpió los envíos a través de su oleoducto este-oeste hacia el mar Rojo. Las cargas se suman a los indicios de una recuperación parcial de los envíos sauditas, y las expectativas de mayores volúmenes lastraron los precios del petróleo el lunes y contribuyeron a que el índice de referencia del Brent cotizara bajo los 100 dólares el barril, por primera vez desde el 9 de septiembre. Los siete buques son petroleros de gran tamaño (VLCC), según TankerTrackers.com. Las imágenes por satélite a las que ha tenido acceso Reuters parecen mostrar siete petroleros cerca del puerto de Ras Tanura, en Arabia Saudita, el domingo. Un portavoz de Aramco no quiso a hacer comentarios. La carga de estos siete petroleros apuntaría a un aumento de los suministros sauditas. Los analistas de JP Morgan señalaron en una nota del 18 de septiembre que los datos satelitales indicaban que el petróleo saudita que atravesaba el estrecho de Ormuz había alcanzado un promedio de 2,9 millones de barriles al día en los últimos seis días, frente a los apenas 700.000 barriles diarios de agosto. Los ataques con drones obligaron a Arabia Saudita a cerrar su oleoducto Este-Oeste el 13 de septiembre, lo que interrumpió las cargas de crudo en el puerto petrolero de Yanbu, situado en el Mar Rojo. Como consecuencia, Aramco canceló algunas ventas de cargamentos de crudo a clientes europeos, al tiempo que incrementó las ventas a Asia del crudo que carga en sus puertos orientales, situados en el estrecho de Ormuz.

item.title: OpenAI pede que EUA assumam liderança nos esforços globais para desenvolver padrões técnicos
item.description: A gigante da inteligência artificial OpenAI pediu nesta segunda-feira que os Estados Unidos liderem um esforço internacional para desenvolver padrões técnicos globais para IA de ponta, incluindo o aprimoramento recursivo, em que os sistemas podem melhorar autonomamente suas próprias capacidades.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A gigante da inteligência artificial OpenAI pediu nesta segunda-feira que os Estados Unidos liderem um esforço internacional para desenvolver padrões técnicos globais para IA de ponta, incluindo o aprimoramento recursivo, em que os sistemas podem melhorar autonomamente suas próprias capacidades. A inteligência artificial será um dos principais temas de discussão na Assembleia Geral da ONU esta semana, após diversos líderes do setor — incluindo Sam Altman, presidente-executivo da OpenAI — pedirem uma desaceleração coordenada no desenvolvimento dessa tecnologia cada vez mais poderosa, alertando que ela poderá em breve se aprimorar sozinha e ficar fora do controle humano. Em uma postagem de blog publicada enquanto líderes mundiais se reuniam nas Nações Unidas, a OpenAI afirmou ser essencial que um mecanismo para facilitar o desenvolvimento de padrões nacionais e internacionais complementares para a vanguarda da IA, juntamente com medições comuns e protocolos de notificação de incidentes para uma melhor ação coletiva. "A liderança agora determinará se os Estados Unidos moldarão a estrutura global da IA ou se assistirão à formação de um sistema fragmentado, desigual e repleto de conflitos. Isso também determinará se a IA avançada fortalecerá as redes que os Estados Unidos e seus aliados já possuem; a falha em liderar pode enfraquecê-las", escreveu a OpenAI em uma postagem de blog na segunda-feira. Diante das preocupações de que a IA possa prejudicar os humanos no futuro, a indústria tem discutido a possibilidade de desacelerar intencionalmente o desenvolvimento, ou "controlar o ritmo". "Ajustar o ritmo do desenvolvimento da IA não significa manter uma velocidade predeterminada. Tecnicamente, trata-se de garantir que a pesquisa alinhada e a implementação dessa pesquisa estejam sempre à frente das capacidades", afirmou a OpenAI. O alinhamento garante que a IA atue em consonância com os valores humanos. CONSELHO DE SEGURANÇA DA ONU SE REUNIRÁ Altman deverá apresentar um relatório aos 15 membros do Conselho de Segurança da ONU na quarta-feira sobre inteligência artificial e segurança internacional. A reunião foi convocada pela França, que preside o órgão em setembro, e será presidida pelo Ministro francês para a Europa e Assuntos Exteriores, Jean-Noël Barrot. O Conselho de Segurança da ONU, encarregado de manter a paz e a segurança internacionais, reuniu-se pela primeira vez em 2023 para discutir os riscos da inteligência artificial, ocasião em que a China afirmou que a tecnologia não deveria se tornar um "descontrole" e os Estados Unidos alertaram contra seu uso para censurar ou reprimir pessoas. O governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, rejeitou os apelos para desacelerar o desenvolvimento da IA, receoso de que qualquer pausa apenas daria à China espaço para reduzir a diferença em uma tecnologia que considera fundamental para a segurança nacional e econômica. Trump afirmou no início deste mês que os EUA já possuem mecanismos de salvaguarda para regulamentar o desenvolvimento da IA, acrescentando que a China se beneficiaria das dúvidas que pairam sobre o desenvolvimento da IA. Trump tem um encontro marcado com o presidente chinês Xi Jinping esta semana em Washington. (Por Michelle Nichols)

item.title: Brazil's Lula meets Mamdani in New York ahead of major elections
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva met New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday for a first chat between two of the biggest names of the political left in the Americas ahead of key elections in both Brazil and the United States.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Teixeira
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva met New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday for a first chat between two of the biggest names of the political left in the Americas ahead of key elections in both Brazil and the United States. Lula is in the US for the United Nations General Assembly and received Mamdani in an Upper East Side house that serves as the residence and office of the Brazilian representation to the UN. Lula said in a brief declaration to reporters after the meeting that the two talked about problems that are common to both countries, particularly the rising cost of living. Mamdani said he would take inspiration from the Brazilian, who had implemented social programs for the poor in Brazil, as he seeks to improve conditions for New Yorkers facing financial pressure for things like groceries and rent. Lula is running for a fourth non-consecutive mandate as Brazil's president with the first round of the vote taking place on October 4. Most polls show him tied with right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the former President Jair Bolsonaro and an ally of US President Donald Trump. Mamdani has been a central figure in the Democratic Party in the US as the country heads to a key mid-term election in November that could change the Congress composition towards a larger representation for the Democrats. Lula and Mamdani exchanged soccer jerseys after the meeting.

item.title: Paramount’s M&A win seals showbiz’s Hamilton fever
item.description: Boss David Ellison is settling with a California-led group that sued to stop its $110 bln deal for Warner Bros, despite federal assent. It took only minor concessions. Tinseltown’s favorite founding father pushed strong national government. In deal policing, he’s gotten his way.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Saba
item.content:encoded: Alexander Hamilton, the first US treasury secretary, is the favorite founding father of show business. Entertainment company Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) owes his vision of a strong central government a debt of gratitude. After receiving the green light from federal antitrust enforcers in Washington, the company has now struck a bargain with state attorneys general who tried to block its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) . It’s a sign of how weak a hand local watchdogs really have. California Attorney General Rob Bonta led the charge, gathering 11 other prosecutors to file suit against the tie-up. They argued that Paramount and Warner Bros together could concentrate power, reduce the number of films released in theaters and ultimately jack up the price of cable packages. The US Department of Justice cleared the deal, as did other international regulatory bodies. The states’ effort was a last-ditch attempt to stop the credits from rolling. Bonta confirmed [USN:L4N45D112 TEXT:"the settlement"] in a press conference on Monday. In return, Paramount has agreed that it will pay a fine if fails to release a promised 30 movies a year, amounting to $30 million per film that misses the target within a five year time frame. Additionally, Paramount has agreed to set up an independent editorial board to oversee the coverage of cable network CNN and broadcaster CBS. Settlements aimed at such finicky behavior-policing have a rough track record. Microsoft (MSFT.O) signed a consent decree with Uncle Sam in 1994 related to its licensing practices. The Department of Justice later sued to break up the software giant, which resulted in another consent decree. Comcast (CMCSA.O) made a similar handshake with regulators when it bought NBC Universal, only for Bloomberg to file a complaint citing anti-competitive conduct. Meta Platforms’ oversight board, implemented to address content grievances, seems to have done little to keep the company out of controversy. Such an exercise in futility is to be expected, given states’ track record. When federal enforcers approved the acquisition of wireless carrier Sprint by T-Mobile US (TMUS.O) , local attorneys again sued to prevent the merger themselves. Their case failed. In this case, Paramount has clinched a denouement to its deal drama just before a crucial October deadline, when it had agreed to start paying fees for further delays. Remarkably, the DOJ effectively [USN:L4N4571N8 TEXT:"backed"] the company’s [USN:FWN44E0IP TEXT:"demand"] that plaintiffs put up a near-$2 billion bond to cover such costs. Much as at the nation’s founding, federalists keep finding ways to exert pressure on the states. Follow Jennifer Saba on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Paramount Skydance has reached a settlement with a group of state attorneys general led by California which sued to block its $110 billion deal with Warner Bros Discovery, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a press conference on September 21. The settlement includes independent editorial boards for the news networks CNN and CBS and a $30 million penalty per film for falling short of Paramount’s promised 30-movies-a-year release target, Reuters reported. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said that "this settlement is not a vote of support for this merger." CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: EUA reafirmam seu apoio a Japão, Coreia do Sul e Taiwan antes da cúpula entre Trump e Xi
item.description: Os Estados Unidos reiteraram, nesta segunda-feira, seu compromisso com a defesa de seus principais aliados asiáticos, o Japão e a Coreia do Sul, e os três países expressaram apoio a Taiwan antes da cúpula desta semana entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o líder chinês, Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: Os Estados Unidos reiteraram, nesta segunda-feira, seu compromisso com a defesa de seus principais aliados asiáticos, o Japão e a Coreia do Sul, e os três países expressaram apoio a Taiwan antes da cúpula desta semana entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o líder chinês, Xi Jinping. Analistas afirmam que os aliados dos EUA estão preocupados com a possibilidade de Trump oferecer concessões a Xi — inclusive em relação a Taiwan e ao comércio — em troca de um ganho econômico com Pequim, quando receber Xi na Casa Branca, em Washington, na quinta-feira. Autoridades afirmam que tanto a primeira-ministra japonesa, Sanae Takaichi, quanto o presidente sul-coreano, Lee Jae Myung, estão ansiosos para se encontrar com o presidente dos EUA durante a Assembleia Geral da ONU em Nova York, onde os três devem discursar na terça-feira. O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, se reuniu com seu homólogo sul-coreano, Cho Hyun, e com o ministro das Relações Exteriores do Japão, Toshimitsu Motegi, em Nova York nesta segunda-feira. Eles emitiram uma declaração conjunta prometendo, em aparente referência à China, manter-se firmes “contra a coerção econômica e políticas e práticas não mercadológicas” e “restrições arbitrárias à exportação que perturbam as cadeias de abastecimento”. Eles também saudaram o lançamento de um novo mecanismo de consulta trilateral sobre segurança econômica, parte de esforços mais amplos para fortalecer as cadeias de abastecimento e a cooperação em tecnologias críticas. A declaração afirmou que os EUA “reiteraram seus compromissos inabaláveis com a defesa do Japão e da ROK, respaldados pelo poderio militar incomparável dos Estados Unidos, incluindo suas capacidades nucleares, e reafirmaram seus compromissos de dissuasão estendida para com o Japão e a ROK”, utilizando as iniciais em inglês da República da Coreia, nome oficial da Coreia do Sul. A declaração afirma que os ministros enfatizaram seu compromisso com uma cooperação robusta em matéria de segurança e a importância de manter a paz e a estabilidade no Estreito de Taiwan. Também “expressaram apoio à participação significativa de Taiwan em organizações internacionais apropriadas”. Referindo-se à Coreia do Norte, os ministros “reafirmaram seu compromisso resoluto com a desnuclearização completa da República Popular Democrática da Coreia” e instaram o país a retomar o diálogo. Além das preocupações com Taiwan, uma ilha governada democraticamente que a China reivindica como sua, analistas afirmaram que os aliados examinarão minuciosamente quaisquer anúncios comerciais da cúpula Trump-Xi quanto ao seu impacto na competitividade em relação à China. Mesmo uma redução modesta nas barreiras comerciais para Pequim poderia minar suas posições. Takaichi irritou Pequim no ano passado ao afirmar que Tóquio poderia ser arrastada para um conflito em torno de Taiwan, e Seul e Washington vêm negociando os detalhes do pacote de investimentos de US$350 bilhões da Coreia do Sul nos Estados Unidos, no âmbito de um acordo comercial firmado pelos aliados no ano passado. Um deputado da oposição sul-coreana pediu, nesta segunda-feira, que o pacote de investimentos fosse analisado pelo Parlamento, alertando que as negociações sobre projetos de energia poderiam fazer com que a Coreia do Sul arcasse com riscos financeiros desproporcionais.

item.title: ロシア与党が過去最多355議席獲得へ、侵攻後初の下院選
item.description:
Andrew Osborn Vladimir Soldatkin
[モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Osborn　Vladimir Soldatkin

[モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] - ロシアで２１日発表された下院選の結果によると、プーチン大統領を支持する与党「統一ロシア」が下院で過去最多となる議席を獲得した。一方、反戦を掲げる野党「ヤブロコ」は、一部地方議会でわずかながら議席を確保したもよう。公式結果はほぼ確定したとみられる。

統一ロシアは、小選挙区の結果も含めて定数４５０議席のうち３５５議席、約８０％を占める見通し。他党の支持なしに法案可決や憲法改正の発議が可能となる憲法上の多数派を維持する。これは、２０１６年の３４３議席という過去最多記録を上回り、史上最多議席となる。

開票率が９５％を超えた時点で、中央選挙管理委員会のパムフィロワ委員長は、統一ロシアの得票率が５７．８３％だったと述べた。前回２０２１年の下院選で獲得した４９．８％を上回った。その他に議会入りしたのは４党で、共産党が１３．８１％、極右の自由民主党（ＬＤＰＲ）が８．９８％、「新しい人々」が７．９６％だった。「公正ロシア」は議会入りに必要な５％をぎりぎりでクリアした。

これら政党は近年、主要な問題では統一ロシアと同じ投票行動を取ってきた。

プーチン大統領は、３日間にわたる下院選を、戦争への支持を測る試金石と位置づけていた。今回はロシアが２０２２年２月にウクライナに侵攻を開始して以来初の下院選となる。一部の地方議会や知事の選挙も同時に実施された。

真の異論を許容しないと批判される厳しく統制された政治体制の下、ヤブロコの候補者の多くが立候補を阻まれており、大きな波乱はほとんど予想されていなかった。

政治アナリストらによると、選挙のプロセス自体が比較的円滑に進んだと見られることは、当局にとって重要だった。プーチン氏をはじめとする当局者は、この選挙をロシアが結束していることを敵に示す手段と位置づけていた。

item.title: A carbon-credit land rush is hollowing out New Zealand farm country
item.dc:creator: Lucy Craymer
item.content:encoded:
At the start of lambing season, Fiona Ramsden’s farm near the New Zealand village of Pongaroa is a picture of rural life: newborn lambs trailing their mothers across steep pasture, fields dotted with spiky native palm trees, and a pretty white homestead that dates back about a century. But pine trees are closing in. On neighboring land once grazed by sheep and cattle, young Monterey pines – also known as radiata pines – carpet the hills, planted to earn carbon credits under the country’s emissions trading scheme. “You’re connected to the land and that’s why it’s quite depressing to see good farmland – and to sheep and beef, good country – going into pine trees,” Ramsden said. Landowner Fiona Ramsden looks out at the pine forests that now run along the property line of her farm outside Pongaroa, New Zealand. REUTERS/Hollie Adams It’s quite depressing to see good farmland – and to sheep and beef, good country – going into pine trees Fiona Ramsden For almost 20 years, New Zealand has pioneered one of the world’s most ambitious tree-planting programs, approving nearly 9,000 square kilometers of carbon-credit forest. That’s about 11 times the land area of New York City. The emissions trading scheme (ETS) has turned forestry into a potentially more lucrative long-term investment than livestock farming, the traditional mainstay of the rural economy. Under the ETS, owners of forests established after 1989 can earn carbon credits for greenhouse gases as their trees grow. Forest owners – companies, indigenous tribal organizations and family farmers with a small slice of land in trees – can sell those carbon credits to companies that need them to offset emissions, creating an income stream long before the forest is harvested. Yet the boom in carbon forestry – and tradable carbon credits – has also driven competition for sheep and beef farming land. The rapid expansion of forest land in traditional beef and sheep country is straining rural communities and prompting the government’s climate advisers to warn that New Zealand is avoiding harder cuts elsewhere in the economy and risks missing its emissions targets. The government counters that forestry remains only one part of its emissions-reduction strategy. Ramsden, 50, returned to take over the family farm in 2012 after a career in fashion and interior design in the capital, Wellington, and elsewhere. Sheep farming has long been the traditional backbone of the rural economy. But the changing economics of land use are challenging its hold. REUTERS/Hollie Adams From her 1,215-hectare property, the tradeoffs of carbon farming feel personal. Pine forests surround her from all sides, barring one block of land. Bright yellow gorse bushes – an invasive plant in New Zealand – tumble toward the fences. Feral goats dart from the forest and onto pasture intended for her 3,500 sheep and 350 cows. Wild pigs tear up patches of ground, problems she says have grown as forest owners do little to control the population. She pointed out a power pole leaning into the pines, noting that she is experiencing more frequent power cuts as trees encroach on powerlines.

For sheep and beef farmer Fiona Ramsden, the arrival of carbon forestry on her doorstep represents a threat to the traditional rural way of life.

WHY TREES BEAT SHEEP Just over half of New Zealand’s greenhouse gas emissions come from agriculture, mainly methane and nitrous oxide. Agricultural emissions are excluded from the ETS, which primarily targets carbon dioxide and emissions from heavy industry . Farmers say that, even so, the ETS has transformed rural land markets. Forestry investors, buoyed by carbon-credit revenue, have been able to outbid sheep and beef producers for grazing land, raising concerns from farm industry groups about the future of traditional beef and sheep farming. Since 2017, about 3,300 square kilometers of sheep and beef farmland have been sold for conversion to forestry, according to industry group Beef + Lamb New Zealand. That’s enough land to feed more than 2 million sheep, equivalent to nearly 9% of the country’s flock. As forestry investors chased carbon credits, grazing land prices rose 9.7%, according to Real Estate Institute of New Zealand data. Digby Thompson, a manager on Ramsden's farm, drives an ATV down a slope of pasture. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Sheep wait to be shorn in a barn in central Hawke’s Bay. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Dairy land, because it’s generally more expensive, has largely escaped forestry conversion and seen price rises of just 3.7%. Foreign investors have acquired more than 1,000 square kilometers of farmland for conversion to forestry since 2017, according to data from the government’s Overseas Investment Office. Ingka Investments, the investment arm of the company that operates most IKEA stores worldwide, owns 430 square kilometers of forest in New Zealand, some of which is in the ETS. Ingka says its rationale is long-term timber, not carbon-credit income. “The heart of our core investment is more in the timber,” said Dylan Foster, forestland operations manager at Ingka Investments. Dylan Foster, forestland operations manager at Ingka Investments, the investment arm of the company that operates most IKEA stores worldwide, inspects a company forests near Porangahau. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Ingka says it is investing in carbon forests for long-term timber, not just carbon-credit income. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Pine forest borders Alex Renner's sheep and beef farm near Pongaroa. REUTERS/Hollie Adams CHEAP CREDITS, HARDER EMISSIONS CUTS Supporters of the ETS say forestry is essential to reaching New Zealand’s climate targets. Climate Change Minister Simon Watts called it a “cost-effective way” to reduce net emissions, because of the country’s established forestry sector and favorable growing conditions. The Climate Change Commission , an independent advisory body, expects ETS forests to deliver a quarter of the emissions reductions needed for New Zealand’s 2026-2030 target, and nearly half of those needed for its 2031-2035 target. But critics say the scheme relies too heavily on offsets, rather than direct emissions cuts. Because planting and maintaining forests is relatively cheap, they say polluters can buy credits rather than make the costlier investments required to transition to cleaner fuels or technology.

A newly planted Ingka forest near the town of Waipukurau. REUTERS/Cordelia Hsu

Climate Change Commission chief executive Jo Hendy said the ETS is essentially “functioning as an offsetting scheme.” The government says New Zealand is on track to meet its near-term climate goals. “Forestry is not the whole plan,” Watts said in response to emailed questions from Reuters. Late last year, the government tightened the ETS rules for non-native species, including pine, on more productive land. Preliminary data released by Beef + Lamb New Zealand last month showed purchases for wholesale conversions had slowed to nearly 160 square kilometers, less than half of the total the year before. However, the industry group said the total could rise once data is finalized. Cattle graze near plantations outside Porangahau, an area that was damaged by wildfires in 2025. REUTERS/Hollie Adams FEWER ANIMALS, FEWER JOBS, THINNER COMMUNITIES For farmer David Buick, high prices for lands suitable for forestry conversion in 2020 offered a chance to trade up to a better farm in the Pongaroa area. “We’ve had to work for every cent we’ve got and so for me it was a good decision to sell that on a forestry high,” he said, while acknowledging the issues of blanket planting of pine trees. But the effects on those left behind ripple beyond the paddock gates. Alex Renner, a sheep and beef farmer who lives about a 10-minute drive from Pongaroa, says he has watched young families leave the area as sheep and beef farms are converted to carbon forestry. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Farmer Alex Renner, who lives a 10-minute drive from Pongaroa, said five neighboring farms had been converted to forestry over the last decade. As more land moved into trees, young families disappeared. The rugby club folded in 2022, after they couldn’t find enough players to field a team. The community-run daycare closed in 2023, in part due to falling enrollment. The population of Owahanga, the rural area that includes Pongaroa, has fallen an estimated 2.6% over the past decade, according to Statistics New Zealand, deepening a decades-long decline driven by reduced demand for rural workers. “We’ve lost a lot of those young families,” Renner said. “It’s people that make a community.” A drone view of Pongaroa, a rural settlement on New Zealand’s North Island about a three-hour drive northeast of Wellington. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Marty Hull, former club captain of the local rugby club in Pongaroa. The club folded in 2022 after it couldn’t find enough players to field a team. REUTERS/Hollie Adams The carbon-credit boom is transforming community life in small towns and villages like Pongaroa. REUTERS/Hollie Adams At a Hawke’s Bay shearing shed, Brandon Coombe-Gray sees the changes one lamb at a time. When farms are planted in pine, fewer ewes mean fewer lambs – and less work for shearers, truck drivers, stock agents and rural contractors. A shearing station that once carried about 10,000 ewes is now planted entirely in pine, he said. “Not one single ewe is there to be seen.” Forestry industry representatives reject the suggestion that the industry hollows out rural regions.The sector provides jobs, supports key industries and generates about NZ$6.5 billion (US$3.7 billion) in annual export earnings, said Elizabeth Heeg, chief executive of the New Zealand Forest Owners Association. Red meat exports generate around NZ$12 billion (US$6.9 billion) in revenue.

Sheep shearer Brandon Coombe-Gray sees the changes one lamb at a time. Fewer ewes mean fewer lambs — and less work for shearers, truck drivers, stock agents and rural contractors, he says.

‘ONE LESS FARM THAT CAN BE BOUGHT’ For some farmers who border forest blocks, downsides include difficulty coordinating with absentee farmers on pest control and damage from goats, deer, pigs and possums moving onto their land. Heeg said that forestry managers “absolutely had active management” of their properties. In 2023, Cyclone Gabrielle – the costliest storm on record in New Zealand – washed forestry debris down waterways in some areas, damaging infrastructure and property. In parts of Hawke’s Bay and Wairarapa, farmers also worry that expanding forest could increase wildfire risks during hot, dry summers. Nateva, one of the largest carbon forest operators in New Zealand, said it runs extensive pest-control and wildfire-prevention programs, removing fire-prone grasses and vegetation from roadsides and tracks. For sheep shearer Axle Reid, the shift to forestry feels like a door closing. The 37-year-old said he had once hoped to save enough from shearing to eventually buy his own place. As more land was converted to forestry and prices rose, he said he felt he’d been pushed out of the market. Watching farmland convert to forestry “feels like a kick in the teeth,” Reid said. “Once they go into forestry, it’s one less farm that can be bought.” Pine trees dot a ridgeline near Porangahau. REUTERS/Hollie Adams

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Puts Global AI Race in Focus
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down what to expect from the Trump-Xi summit later this week, with AI's role anticipated to be a major part of the agenda for those upcoming talks. Plus, Bloomberg reports Paramount reached a settlement with California and other states suing to block its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. And, as data shows more disruption to US data centers, we get to the political debate with Democratic US Representative Suhas Subramanyam from Virginia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Takes on Apple, Microsoft With AI-Powered Laptops
item.description: Google is taking another shot at the premium laptop market with its Googlebooks, priced at $899 and built around Gemini AI and with tighter integration with Android phones. Sameer Samat, president of the Android Ecosystem at Google, explains why the company combined elements of Android and ChromeOS for the new experience and how some of the new features are designed to challenge Apple and Microsoft in the AI PC race. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Congressman Calls for National Data Center Strategy
item.description: Democratic Rep. Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia is calling for a national strategy to guide the rapid expansion of AI data centers, arguing the current state-by-state approach can leave communities bearing infrastructure costs. He discusses proposals to improve where data centers are built, measure their energy and water use, and require large electricity users to cover the grid upgrades needed to serve them. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Agropalma vê alta de 20% na nova safra após El Niño de 2023 afetar ciclo passado
item.description: A Agropalma, líder na fabricação de óleo de palma do Brasil, projeta um aumento de cerca de 20% na produção da safra que se inicia em relação à anterior, após ter sido atingida no ano passado pelos efeitos do El Niño de 2023 e 2024, disse um diretor da companhia à Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Samora
item.content:encoded: A Agropalma, líder na fabricação de óleo de palma do Brasil, projeta um aumento de cerca de 20% na produção da safra que se inicia em relação à anterior, após ter sido atingida no ano passado pelos efeitos do El Niño de 2023 e 2024, disse um diretor da companhia à Reuters. A palma, cultivada na Amazônia brasileira, leva duas safras para refletir mais fortemente os efeitos das altas temperaturas e redução de chuvas decorrentes do fenômeno climático, o que explica o aumento esperado para 2026, ainda que este seja um ano de El Niño. A situação sinaliza ainda que o fenômeno climático de 2026/27, que pode ser um dos mais fortes da história, poderia impactar a produção nos próximos anos da empresa e de outros operadores do setor, concentrado no Pará -- o Norte do país geralmente enfrenta tempo mais seco e quente em anos de El Niño. "Enquanto a maior parte do mundo usa o termo 'climate change', a gente aqui prefere 'climate disorder'... para nós aqui, o que está acontecendo que é muito visível: é uma modificação em todo o regime climático, não só de chuvas, como de temperatura", disse o diretor Agrícola da Agropalma, André Borba. Embora seja uma potência agrícola e grande parte do país esteja localizada na faixa tropical do planeta, o Brasil é um importador de óleo de palma, já que grande parte de sua produção de óleo vegetal vem da soja. Oscilações na oferta brasileira, que normalmente gira em torno de 600 mil toneladas de óleo de palma por ano, poderiam impactar as importações, estimadas em [USN:L1N43N15V TEXT:"cerca de 30%"] do consumo anual de 1 milhão de toneladas. A última boa safra da Agropalma, que responde por um quarto da produção nacional, foi a de 2022, disse Borba, citando impactos de El Niños passados. Ele explicou que o cacho de frutos da palma colhido em 2026 é formado dois anos antes. "Então, se nós temos um estresse hídrico, estresse de temperatura ou de umidade, ao invés de a palmeira produzir uma inflorescência feminina que vai virar o cacho, ela produz uma masculina que não vira produção." "No ano de 2024, nós tivemos bastante problema com falta de chuva e com aumento de temperatura, que de certa maneira estão prejudicando este ano. Mas o ano de 2025 sofreu mais ainda por conta do ano de 2023", ressaltou. Apesar de o clima ter desafiado a produção nos últimos anos, o Brasil tem potencial para mais do que triplicar o plantio de palma de óleo em um período de dez anos, utilizando áreas desmatadas anteriormente na Amazônia, com impulso da demanda por matérias-primas para a produção de biocombustíveis avançados como o SAF de aviação, afirmou o presidente da Associação Brasileira de Produtores de Óleo de Palma (Abrapalma), Victor Almeida, em entrevista recente à Reuters. Borba preferiu não comentar sobre planos de expansão da Agropalma, adquirida este ano pelo grupo [USN:L1N3ZS1EI TEXT:"colombiano Daabon"], que passou a ter uma fatia majoritária na empresa. No processo produtivo, a companhia usa 75% de frutos de produção própria, comprando o restante de terceiros, incluindo agricultores familiares. NOVA SAFRA A Agropalma está perto de iniciar a colheita nos meses que registram maiores produtividades. Os maiores volumes de colheita de frutos são em outubro, com cerca de 12% da produção no ano, novembro, com 15%, e dezembro, com 10%, disse o diretor Agrícola da Agropalma. Em abril, normalmente são os menores volumes, próximos de 4%. "É uma planta que depende bastante do clima. Ela não produz em áreas com temperaturas baixas e tampouco produz em áreas com pouca chuva. Então, ela demanda mais ou menos 150 milímetros de chuva por mês... essa é a razão de nós estarmos aqui na região Norte, mais próximo da linha do Equador, que é uma das regiões que mais chove no Brasil...", explicou. Sob a influência do El Niño, contudo, ele disse acreditar que as temperaturas mais altas terão maior influência na safra do que a escassez de chuvas. "A temperatura média este ano está mais ou menos 29 graus (Celsius), dois graus acima do normal. As máximas, que geralmente chegam a 32 graus, este ano estão chegando a 36." Ele disse ter expectativa de que o El Niño afete a lavoura até fevereiro do próximo ano, já que o fenômeno deverá adiar as chuvas que normalmente voltam a se intensificar na região em dezembro, estendendo-se até junho. Para lidar com o problema, Borba destacou que a companhia adota a puerária, uma leguminosa, como cobertura verde, o que reduz a temperatura do solo de 54 graus para 23. "Com essa temperatura bem menor, nós conseguimos manter mais umidade no solo e nosso plantio sofre menos com os efeitos da falta de chuva e da temperatura." A puerária tem ainda a capacidade de captar o nitrogênio da atmosfera, fixando-o no solo, o que permite redução de custos com adubação. Além disso, a leguminosa atrai insetos predadores de pragas, dispensando o uso de pesticidas químicos.

item.title: BID elabora plano de dois anos para a Venezuela e diz que setor elétrico e áreas sociais são fundamentais
item.description: O Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento está elaborando um plano de atuação de dois anos para a Venezuela, com foco parcial nos setores de energia elétrica e proteção social, afirmou nesta segunda-feira o presidente do BID, Ilan Goldfajn.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: O Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento está elaborando um plano de atuação de dois anos para a Venezuela, com foco parcial nos setores de energia elétrica e proteção social, afirmou nesta segunda-feira o presidente do BID, Ilan Goldfajn. “Estamos, é claro, retomando nosso envolvimento”, disse Goldfajn em entrevista à Reuters. “Temos missões na Venezuela para analisar a situação, lidar com o quadro macroeconômico, examinar os dados e elaborar uma nota de compromisso — um documento no qual possamos definir o que planejamos fazer nos próximos dois anos.” O BID é a maior instituição financeira de desenvolvimento da América Latina e do Caribe e conta com 48 países-membros, incluindo 26 membros mutuários na região. O banco suspendeu a concessão de novos empréstimos à Venezuela em maio de 2018, após o país ter atrasado pagamentos, e ainda possui cerca de US$2 bilhões em empréstimos venezuelanos pendentes. Goldfajn não informou como os atrasos da Venezuela serão resolvidos nem quando o financiamento poderá ser retomado. “Ainda estamos na fase de planejamento e trabalho com os venezuelanos, mantendo contato e visitando as missões, para ver como podemos trabalhar com eles”, disse ele. Questionado se o BID está preparando sua própria análise de sustentabilidade da dívida para a Venezuela, Goldfajn disse que, em vez disso, o banco estava se concentrando no quadro macroeconômico do país e nas necessidades de cada setor.
